core.title: Every feature that owns behaviour to deliver has source beneath its feature directory
core.given: A feature in the plan owns one or more plan artifacts that specify behaviour to deliver.
core.when: The topology gate checks that feature's directory in the source tree.
core.then: At least one source component exists beneath the feature's directory for every feature that owns plan behaviour.
prefer: Implement the feature beneath its own feature directory.
If another feature actually delivers the behaviour, reassign the plan artifacts to that feature in the plan.
avoid: Leaving a feature that owns behaviour to deliver with no implementation (a gap the plan already names).
Satisfying the check with source placed only in vendored or generated trees; those are never scanned.
core.why: A feature with behaviour to deliver and no implementation is a gap the plan already names.
evidence: The topology coverage check reports no feature that owns plan behaviour without a source component beneath its feature directory.
The rule's failing fixture (a feature owning plan behaviour with no source component) is rejected by the stack's guard.
verification: For each feature that owns at least one behaviour-specifying plan artifact, require at least one source component beneath the feature's directory.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact trees are the stack's single never-scanned list from the profile, and source found only there does not satisfy the check.
Resolve the topology roots from the repository's declared configuration; the rule hard-codes no path.
Disposition strict, severity 3; a violation fails the gate.

values: any file beneath the plan root
any file beneath a feature directory (any product capability's feature tree)
behaviour-specifying plan artifact added to or moved between features
a feature owns behaviour-specifying plan artifacts but has no source component

fires: A feature in the plan owns one or more behaviour-specifying plan artifacts and its feature directory holds no source component.
A change deletes or moves the last source component out of a feature directory whose feature still owns plan behaviour.
The only source beneath a feature that owns plan behaviour sits in vendored or generated trees (the stack's never-scanned list).
doesNotFire: A feature that owns no plan behaviour has no source directory.
A feature that owns plan behaviour has at least one source component beneath its feature directory.
Changes confined to vendored or generated trees (never scanned).

Root of end-to-end tests; declared in the same topology configuration this rule resolves its roots from, though this coverage check itself does not use it.
Directory of one feature inside its product capability: the tree the coverage check scans for a source component.

The file in which the repository declares its topology roots.

The Bun path_glob fact covers every file beneath the plan root (<plan_root>/**) and every file beneath any feature directory of any product capability (<source_root>/*/features/*/**). The core keeps that full scope with the neutral file_kind fact ('any file beneath the plan root', 'any file beneath a feature directory'); the profile's plan root and feature-directory pattern reconstruct the concrete globs when instantiated.

neutralityNotes: 'DESIRED OUTCOME' is the stack's plan-artifact kind for behaviour to deliver; the core always says 'plan artifact that specifies behaviour to deliver' and takes the concrete kind from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The Bun activation fact type path_glob has no neutral counterpart in the closed fact vocabulary (role|operation|change|phase|finding|file_kind|task_term|task_has_acceptance), so it is re-typed as file_kind with values that keep the full scope: every file beneath the plan root and every file beneath a feature directory, restored to the exact globs by roots.plan and layout.feature_dir when the Bun profile is applied. The never-scanned tree names are the stack-wide roots.excluded list, so the core defers the exact classification to that single list. The validator id (`atdd_topology`), the config file (`atdd-bun.yaml`) and its `topology:` key spellings stay in the Bun realization; the root values themselves, including the test and e2e roots this coverage check does not use, are profile data (roots.plan, roots.source, roots.test, roots.e2e).
